advisory.finding: The overlap matcher (token-set Jaccard >= 0.5 over the full finding text) is too strict for findings that say the same thing in different words. The recorded run matches 1 of about 160 findings even where both engines plainly report the same defect. The reported overlap cannot tell real engine disagreement apart from the matcher failing, and no calibration against known paraphrase pairs backs the threshold.
scenarios: An operator reads 'matched: 1' as the engines finding almost entirely different defects, when the matcher simply could not pair paraphrases.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drive the retry test through `_Scripted` raising a retryable provider exception, instead of monkeypatching `ec._review_once`, and add an assertion that a non-retryable error does not sleep or retry
evidence: tests/unit/test_engine_comparison.py:232: monkeypatch.setattr(ec, "_review_once", fake_review)
src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:302-304: if result["outcome"] == "error" and result.get("class") in RETRYABLE: sleep(RETRY_DELAY_S); result = _review_once(...)

tests/unit/test_engine_comparison.py:95: kw.setdefault("sleep", lambda s: None) — the error-path tests (test_errors_and_floor_rows_are_excluded_not_disagreements, test_resume_reviews_errored_rows_again) never check that sleep was not called for the NEEDS_INVESTIGATION RuntimeError
advisory.finding: The retry test replaces the module's own private `_review_once` instead of having the runner raise a retryable provider error. As a result, the real path that classifies an exception as WAIT_AND_RETRY or RETRY_NOW and then retries is never run. No test checks the opposite case either: a non-retryable error (NEEDS_INVESTIGATION) must not be retried or trigger a sleep.
scenarios: Renaming `_review_once` or changing its signature breaks the test even though behaviour is unchanged.
If classify_outcome or _resolution_class stopped mapping a throttling exception to WAIT_AND_RETRY, the retry would silently stop happening and this test would stay green.
If the RETRYABLE guard were widened so every error was retried, no test would fail.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the error-path tests, pass `sleep=slept.append` and assert `slept == []` for the RuntimeError case. For the retry case, have `_Scripted` raise an exception that `failure.classify_llm_failure` maps to WAIT_AND_RETRY on its first call and succeed on the second, then assert `slept == [ec.RETRY_DELAY_S]` and that the outcome is PASS.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a summarize() table test that includes a historical INDETERMINATE row and an excluded row with non-zero overlap, and assert the exact summary['overlap'] and historical_pipeline_agreement values
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:175: elif item["historical_pipeline_verdict"] in DECIDED:
src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:164-165: for key, value in item["overlap"].items(): overlap[key] += value

Absence: none of the summary assertions in tests/unit/test_engine_comparison.py (lines 111-120, 126-129, 293) reads summary["overlap"], and every test row uses historical verdict PASS or BLOCK (the _row(...) calls at lines 108, 124, 143, 200, 207)
advisory.finding: No test reaches two branches of summarize: (1) items whose historical verdict is not PASS or BLOCK are left out of historical_pipeline_agreement, and (2) overlap totals are summed across compared items only. No test asserts summary['overlap'] or a historical n that is smaller than the number of decided items. The committed results file depends on both, for example historical agreement over n=10 of 11 rows.
scenarios: Input: items=[{pipeline:{outcome:'PASS'}, agentic:{outcome:'PASS'}, overlap:{matched:0,pipeline_only:0,agentic_only:0}, historical_pipeline_verdict:'INDETERMINATE'}] should give historical {'agree':0,'n':0}. If the DECIDED guard were dropped, the result would be n=1 and no test would fail.
If overlap were summed over all items, including excluded ones, or not summed at all, every test would still pass.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a pure summarize() test with three items: one compared item (overlap {1,2,3}), one item where one engine has outcome 'error' (overlap {5,5,5}), and one compared item with historical 'INDETERMINATE'. Assert that overlap equals only the compared items' sum and that historical n counts only the PASS/BLOCK historical rows.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Isolate the engines: give each engine its own case_store, or remove .rebar/cache/plan-review/<tid> between engine runs, then re-record engine_comparison_results.json
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:278: `with eval_solver.case_store({"files": files}) as store:` creates ONE store per row.

src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:300-301: `for engine in ENGINES: result = _review_once(tid, engine, store, cfg, runner)`. ENGINES = ("pipeline", "agentic"), so the pipeline always runs first on the same tid and store.

src/rebar/llm/plan_review/checkpoints.py:37: `return Path(ctx.repo_root) / ".rebar" / "cache" / "plan-review" / ctx.ticket_id`. save_checkpoint writes the pipeline's Pass-1 envelopes under the store root, whatever sign/emit_sidecar are set to.

src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/engine_comparison_results.json:154: an agentic finding says `EXIT_RESCHEDULE and _FIELD_WEIGHTS also appear nowhere outside the .rebar review cache`, so the agent read the cache.
src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/engine_comparison_results.json:222: an agentic finding says `the heading text appears nowhere except old review-cache JSON`.
blocking.finding: Both engines review the same ticket in one shared disposable store, always pipeline first. The pipeline's Pass-1 checkpoint files (.rebar/cache/plan-review/<tid>/*.json) are therefore still in the store when the agentic engine runs, and the agent's file tools can read them. That breaks the independence the comparison depends on and adds a fixed order bias.
scenarios: The agentic engine greps the store and reads the pipeline's checkpointed Pass-1 findings or material, which raises its apparent agreement with the pipeline or shapes its findings.
Cache artifacts show up as evidence in agentic findings, as in the committed results, which skews the recorded comparison.
blocking.suggested_fix: Inside review_row, open a fresh `eval_solver.case_store` (and create the ticket, set file impact and build cfg/runner) per engine, so neither engine can see the other's checkpoints. Alternatively, `shutil.rmtree(Path(store)/'.rebar'/'cache'/'plan-review', ignore_errors=True)` before each `_review_once`. Then re-run and commit fresh results.
